newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's coffee income seen off sharply in '96.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's coffee income seen off sharply in '96.

text.p: Colombia will suffer a 14.6 percent drop in coffee revenues this year thanks to soaring production costs and the strengthening of the country's peso currency, the head of the Colombian Farmers' Association (SAC) said Thursday.

Juan Manuel Ospina, speaking at a forum on the crisis in Colombia's agricultural sector, said real income from the country's coffee output was expected to total no more than 14.9 billion pesos this year, compared to 17.4 billion in 1995.

As with most of the farming sector, he said coffee growers were being squeezed by rising production costs stemming from inflation, which is expected to total at least 21 percent this year, and high domestic interest rates.
The recent appreciation of the peso, which was trading at more than 1,070 to the dollar in June and closed Wednesday at 993.54, has also put a serious strain on the coffee industry, Ospina said.
The rising peso makes Colombian goods less attractive in the global marketplace and erodes the real value of export revenues once they are converted back into local currency.
Ospina said the farming sector as a whole was expected to grow by no more than than 0.1 percent in 1996 compared to bubbling 5.3 percent growth rate in 1995.
